pool.text: Arthur Wellesley became the first Duke of Wellington and victor of the battle.
Colonel William Wakefield arrived to purchase land for the New Zealand Company.
Captain William Mein Smith designed the original form of Wellington city layout.
The Wellington Borough Council was established as the first local government.
The oldest building became the Nairn Street Cottage in Mount Cook.
The capital was moved to Wellington and officially met in session.
Wellington hosted the New Zealand Centennial Exhibition celebrating a century.
The Wairarapa earthquakes caused considerable damage in Wellington city.
The Johnsonville Town District was annexed by Wellington city.
Television broadcasts began with the launch of channel WNTV1 in the city.
The Mount Victoria transmitter was replaced with a more powerful transmitter at Mount Kaukau.
The Executive Wing of New Zealand Parliament Buildings was constructed.
WNTV1 was networked with counterpart stations to form NZBC TV in November.
Wellington was supplied with natural gas when the Kapuni field produced.
The NZBC was broken up, with Wellington and Dunedin studios taking over Television One.
Televisions One and Two merged under a single company known as Television New Zealand.
Production culminated in the opening of TVNZ's new Auckland television centre.
The restored Government Buildings near Parliament became the largest wooden building.
The two newspapers merged to form The Dominion Post newspaper.
The New Zealand School of Music was established through a merger.
